remaining_concerns: The affected developer-support migration segment remains below target and is still exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
The 7% rollout gate does not exclude the affected segment.
There is no approved risk-acceptance record that specifically covers the continued exposure.
The cited policy states rollout controls and post-launch monitoring mitigate a material model-card weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or covered by reviewed risk acceptance.

The record provided here does not include a final model-card/disclosure artifact showing the limitation is explicitly documented; even if it did, disclosure alone would not satisfy the certification predicate while exposure remains.
final_rationale: The verdict does not change. No new admissible evidence was provided; the Actor expressly offered none and mainly reframed the same record more narrowly. That reframing is partially valid in one respect: it correctly concedes that aggregate readiness, lack of severity-one incidents, staged rollout, rollback, and monitoring do not by themselves satisfy the governing policy when the affected segment remains exposed. But that concession does not improve the compliance outcome. The policy text is explicit that rollout controls and monitoring can mitigate this weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or there is reviewed risk acceptance explaining why exposure is acceptable. On the available evidence summary, neither condition is met. This is the key distinction between a narrowed caveated position and actual compliant certification: a caveat can prevent overstatement, but it cannot satisfy an unresolved compliance predicate. Because the certification claim still depends on conditions not shown by admissible evidence, the current record remains noncompliant.
